record.paper_title: A New Paradigm for Scattering Theory of Linear and Nonlinear Waves: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: Do existing small-data inverse nonlinear scattering results for nonlinear Schrödinger equations with potentials and polynomial nonlinearities hold in sufficient generality to determine complex nonlinear systems from small scattering experiments, and can large-data free-channel wave operators or free-to-free scattering matrices recover the Born-type information needed to determine the interaction terms?

evidence.quote: Therefore, if it can be shown that the Born approximation is uniquely determined by the Free Channel Wave Operator or by the free-to-free Scattering matrix, the results follow.

The first question of interest is whether the above results hold in sufficient generality. This would be significant, implying that small data scattering experiments can determine the complex structure of nonlinear systems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider nonlinear Schrödinger equations on $\mathbb{R}^d$ of the form
$$ i\partial_t u(t,x) = (-\Delta + V(x)) u(t,x) + N(x,u(t,x)), \qquad (t,x) \in \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^d, $$
where $V$ is a (real-valued, sufficiently decaying) external potential and $N(x,u)$ is a polynomial-type nonlinearity, e.g. $N(x,u) = \sum_{k} \lambda_k(x) |u|^{2 p_k} u$ with unknown coefficient functions $\lambda_k(x)$.

For small initial data $u(0,\cdot) = \varphi$ in a suitable space, the solution scatters and one can define:
(i) the free-channel wave operator $W_+:\varphi \mapsto u_+$, where $u_+$ is the asymptotic free profile so that $\|u(t)-e^{-it(-\Delta+V)}u_+\|\to 0$ as $t\to+\infty$ (or its analogue with $-\Delta$ in place of $-\Delta+V$);
(ii) the free-to-free scattering matrix $S:\varphi_- \mapsto \varphi_+$, mapping incoming to outgoing asymptotic free profiles.

The associated Born approximation is the leading-order nonlinear correction extracted from $W_+$ or $S$ as the amplitude of the data tends to zero; formally it encodes the multilinear form determined by $N$ and $V$.

Address the following:

(a) Do the known small-data inverse scattering results — which reconstruct $V$ and the coefficients of the polynomial nonlinearity $N$ from the small-data asymptotics of $W_+$ or $S$ — extend to a class of nonlinearities and potentials sufficiently general that small-data scattering measurements uniquely determine the full nonlinear interaction (i.e., both $V$ and $N$) for a "generic" nonlinear Schrödinger system?

(b) In the large-data regime, assuming the free-channel wave operator $W_+$ (respectively the free-to-free scattering matrix $S$) is defined globally, is the Born approximation uniquely determined by $W_+$ (respectively by $S$)? Equivalently, can one recover from the large-data map $W_+$ (or $S$) the multilinear/Born-type data sufficient to identify $V$ and the interaction terms in $N$?
artifact.status_search_result: Inverse scattering via the Born approximation is well developed for linear and small-data nonlinear Schrödinger problems (full, backscattering, fixed-angle and fixed-energy data), and partial results recover singularities of unknown potentials/nonlinearities. However, no source found establishes the general statement that large-data free-channel wave operators or free-to-free scattering matrices determine the Born approximation, nor that small-data results hold in the full generality needed to identify arbitrary complex nonlinear systems. The problem is posed as an open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Direct and inverse scattering for nonlinear Schrödinger equation in 2D
status_evidence.snippet: Main singularities of an unknown potential can be recovered from the Born approximation in 2D NLS.
status_evidence.claim: Small-data Born-type recovery results exist but are limited in generality.

status_evidence.title: A Recursive Born Approach to Nonlinear Inverse Scattering
status_evidence.snippet: Higher-order Born approximations account for multiple scattering beyond the linearized regime.
status_evidence.claim: Recovery beyond the small-data/first-Born regime remains an active research problem.

status_evidence.title: Inverse Scattering Transform for NLS: Survey and Future Directions
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys classical results and identifies open directions for inverse scattering for NLS systems.
status_evidence.claim: The generality and large-data versions of inverse nonlinear scattering remain open.
